metadata.title: The Universe of Knobs
metadata.description:
A popular-technical picture book: 169 pages, 130 figures. AI-assisted; not peer reviewed; no outside group has reproduced the numbers it quotes. The coefficient κ = 1/2 is fitted, not derived. The galaxy law is Milgrom's modified dynamics in its simple form, and the tie of its scale to the dark energy density was proposed by Limbach, Psaltis and Özel (2008). The theory is not closed: it fails in galaxy clusters, supplies nothing for the cosmic microwave background, and fails the other tests listed in chapter 12. Nothing here says the data favour this framework over ΛCDM.

The book counts free parameters, which it calls knobs. Part I explains knobs mathematically (degrees of freedom, AIC and BIC, Bayesian evidence and the Occam factor, knobs measured in bits) and gives base ΛCDM's six-parameter fit to the microwave background its due. Part II walks through the working note ACDM flavored fried chicken version of Galaxy Dynamics (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23962973): four ΛCDM knobs reproduce the law's acceleration scale, twelve supernova-feedback knobs land 0.0415 dex from the law, a 26-knob recipe fails four of nine frozen lines, about 1066 parameters make only a patchwork, and no ΛCDM route ties the scale to the dark energy density without terms written in by hand. Part III looks at the string landscape (10^500 vacua, about 1661 bits). Part IV sets out the one-knob galaxy law, its wins on disc galaxies and its full failure record from PAPER67 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23966443). Part V presents the prediction with no galaxy knob left in it, a0(z)/a0(0) = sqrt(ρ_DE(z)/ρ_DE(0)), with the published MUSE-DARK III rise that counts against it at face value and the measurements that could decide it.

Every quoted number is checked against the two source papers by the book's audit script. Figures, worked numbers and the LaTeX source are in the programme's public repository (folder book_universe_of_knobs). Illustrations are drawings, not data; cartoons and mock data are labelled on the figure.
